description: Know what your inbox needs from you. Gmail Sentry triages new mail against rules you write in plain language, tracks the threads you owe people and the ones that have gone quiet, files whole conversations into folders you approve, and drafts replies in your own voice — you approve, it sends.

sections.label: Triage & alerts
sections.description: Starting defaults for a new user. Everything here can be changed later in the app on the Rules screen, which then owns the value.

fields.label: Ping me about
fields.description: Which mail is worth interrupting you for.

options.label: Urgent only
options.description: Only mail Sentry classifies as urgent.

options.label: Urgent + needs a reply
options.description: Also ping for mail that's waiting on an answer from you.

fields.label: Draft replies automatically
fields.description: Write a reply in your voice as soon as mail is flagged, so the notification carries a ready-to-send draft. Nothing is ever sent without your approval.

sections.label: Organizing
sections.description: Filing settings. Folders are always proposed for your approval first — nothing is created in your mailbox without a yes.

fields.label: File conversations into folders
fields.description: Suggest a folder for each new conversation, based on who it's with. Nothing is filed until you approve the folder, and filing never removes mail from your inbox.

features: Tells you what you owe people and who has gone quiet — the silences that cost you customers
Chase a thread that's gone quiet with a short follow-up in your voice — you approve every one, and it won't let you over-chase
Teach it in plain language what matters; it turns your words into rules, grounded in your real inbox
AI triage of incoming Gmail into urgent / needs-reply / FYI, with the actual ask pulled out in one line
Learns who matters from how you really behave — who you answer, how fast — not from who emails most, and lets you correct it when it's wrong
Files whole conversations into folders you approve, your replies included, so a thread lives in one place
One-tap replies written in your own voice, learned from your real sent mail
Nothing ever sends without you — every reply shows the recipient before it goes
Notice replies you sent from your phone, so the app never nags about mail you already handled
A daily report of what needs answering, what's going quiet, and what got filed
Alerts on Slack, WhatsApp, Telegram or Discord — with a ready-to-send reply attached
One-tap bulk clear of Promotions, Social and Spam

how_to_capture: Run `cd frontend && npm run screenshots` — regenerates every declared file at 2x from the live widget.
Re-run it after any widget change; the PNGs are build output, not hand-captured art.
best_practices: Element screenshots at deviceScaleFactor 2 — exactly 170×170 / 360×170 / 360×360 at 2x, no page chrome.
Data comes from frontend/tests/fixtures/widget-marketing.json: plausible people, companies and asks.
The fixture uses pre-rendered relative strings ('4m ago'), so re-running gives byte-identical files.
Never ship 'test'/'foo'/'lorem'/'example.com'/'John Doe' — obvious placeholder data reads as unfinished.

core_action.definition_of_done: A new email that needs a reply arrives; within a scan the user gets a notification on their channel carrying a reply drafted in their own voice and a one-tap approve link. Tapping it lands on the email with Approve & Send, which really sends through Gmail in-thread — or shows a clear connect-Gmail prompt when an integration isn't connected, never a faked success. The thread then stays visible as an open loop waiting on them rather than disappearing, and surfaces as going cold if they never answer. A reply the user sends from their phone closes the alert on its own. Conversations are filed into folders the user approved — their own replies included — and nothing is ever labelled with a folder they haven't approved. A daily report says what needs answering, who has gone quiet, and what was filed.
